convertibility_reason: Martingale position sizing with factor-based volume increase per level, grid-like step-based position stacking, and margin-dependent volume checking via CTrade.CheckVolume. The strategy inherently relies on sequential position opening at price steps which requires precise margin tracking and broker-dependent lot validation that cannot be reliably replicated in Python backtesting.

Close all positions when both buy and sell positions exist simultaneously (error condition)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: Lot = InpLots * MathPow(InpIncreaseFactor, count_buys_or_count_sells), capped at InpMaxLot. Volume validated by LotCheck (normalized to step, min/max checked) and CTrade.CheckVolume (margin check). Position only opened if lot != 0.0 and lot < InpMaxLot.

custom_logic_notes: Martingale/grid hybrid EA for small deposits. Opens first position based on 15-bar price trend comparison (close[1] vs close[15]). Subsequent positions added at ExtStep price intervals with exponentially increasing volume (factor^count). Bars-skipped counter tracks how many bars since last deal; new positions only added when skipped bars exceed InpBarsSkipped threshold. All positions closed when total profit (including swap and commission) exceeds InpMinProfit. Mixed buy/sell positions trigger emergency close-all. No stop loss on individual positions - exit is purely profit-target based on aggregate portfolio. TP is set per-position but the real exit is the profit-target close-all.
python_conversion_notes: Core martingale sizing logic (InpLots * factor^N) is straightforward to convert. However, the margin-check via CTrade.CheckVolume has no direct Python equivalent and must be approximated or omitted. The grid-step re-entry logic (price distance > ExtStep) requires tracking open positions and their prices. The bars-skipped counter logic (CopyOpen from last deal time) needs careful bar-index handling. The TP on individual positions is redundant since exit is profit-target based. Digit adjustment (5-digit broker handling) must be replicated. The filling type detection (FOK/IOC/RETURN) is broker-dependent and not applicable in Python backtesting. No technical indicators used, so no indicator conversion needed.
